metadata.result_basis: illustrative gross insurer payouts before reinsurance

curve_provenance.summary: Provisional fixture curves. Every damage fraction below is ASSUMED. No curve here is measured, calibrated or validated against loss experience.
curve_provenance.baseline_derivation: Baseline pre-FBC fractions are the platform's already-published vulnerability assumption (risk.wind_damage_ratio: min(0.85, 0.9 * ((kt - 50) / 100) ** 2.2), sustained knots) evaluated on this file's gust grid using kt = mph / (1.15078 * 1.30). Reusing it keeps one vulnerability assumption in the product rather than two competing ones.
curve_provenance.upgrade_derivation: Upgrade curves are the baseline scaled by (1 - effectiveness) using the hurricane effectiveness already published on /api/meta/model: opening-protection 0.25 for 'shutters', roof-to-wall 0.20 for 'roof_straps'. This is an assumed uniform effect across all wind speeds, which is almost certainly wrong in shape: real mitigation effects vary with intensity.
curve_provenance.code_uplift_derivation: post_fbc_2002 baseline is pre_fbc_2002 scaled by 0.60, an assumed uplift for homes built to the 2002 Florida Building Code. Not sourced.
curve_provenance.finance_workbook_status: StormShield_Finance_Data_v5.xlsx returned NO damage-effect evidence: 'Data Request - Upgrades' tables A and B have every Answer cell blank ('—'), under an explicit ground rule that a premium discount must not be converted into a damage reduction. These fixtures exist so the engine can run before that request is answered; they are not a substitute for it.
curve_provenance.do_not: Do not present these as FORTIFIED, IBHS or study-derived results. Replace this whole file when the math/research team supplies curves.

curve_source_notes.pre_fbc_2002.baseline.assumed.v1: Assumed. Platform vulnerability curve risk.wind_damage_ratio on the gust grid. Single-family home built before the 2002 Florida Building Code.
curve_source_notes.pre_fbc_2002.shutters.assumed.v1: Assumed. Baseline x 0.75 (opening-protection hurricane effectiveness 0.25). Scope: whole-house accordion shutters on every opening, per Finance workbook row 'Hurricane shutters — accordion, whole-house'.
curve_source_notes.pre_fbc_2002.roof_straps.assumed.v1: Assumed. Baseline x 0.80 (roof-to-wall hurricane effectiveness 0.20). Scope: roof-to-wall strap/clip retrofit on an existing roof. Finance workbook flags the sourced price at $850-$5,000, not the $20,000 the starter model assumed.
curve_source_notes.post_fbc_2002.baseline.assumed.v1: Assumed. pre_fbc_2002 baseline x 0.60 code-uplift factor. Single-family home built to the 2002 Florida Building Code or later.
curve_source_notes.post_fbc_2002.shutters.assumed.v1: Assumed. post_fbc_2002 baseline x 0.75. No roof_straps curve exists for this class: roof-to-wall connections are already required by the 2002 code, so the retrofit is not an eligible option and must not be offered.

metadata.sampling_description: hurricane_simulator V1 Monte Carlo run of 1000 synthetic Atlantic storms bootstrapped from HURDAT2 1851-2025 at a 6-hour time step. This catalog holds hand-picked storm ids SYN0155, SYN0697, SYN0973. Track points are clipped to lat 18.0 to 35.0, lon -92.0 to -72.0.

policy_basis.note: A percentage deductible is applied to Coverage A, never to damage.

wind_model.gust_factor_note: ASSUMED ratio of a 3-second gust to the simulator's one-minute sustained wind, over open terrain: wind_field's demonstration value, agreed for the platform. Not calibrated.

storm_parameters.rmw_form: ln(rmw_km) = intercept + per_kt * max_wind_kt + per_degree_latitude * latitude

fit.dataset: NOAA NHC HURDAT2 Atlantic best track

wind_model.storm_parameters_note: Storm size per storm from the storm-size model fitted to HURDAT2 wind radii: the radius of maximum wind from the storm's peak intensity and latitude, decay and taper from record-wide medians, constant within each event. The per-storm values used are in metadata.storm_size. Parameters are constant within each event: evaluated once per storm at its peak-intensity track point. The profile is axisymmetric; forward-motion asymmetry and land effects are not represented.
wind_model.method: For each property, the peak over the whole track of: the storm centre moved along great circles in steps of at most max_time_step_minutes and max_segment_distance_fraction_rmw x rmw_km; at each step, sustained wind from a modified-Rankine profile (max_wind_kt x r/rmw inside the radius of maximum wind, max_wind_kt x (rmw/r)^outer_decay_exponent outside it, cosine-tapered to zero between taper_start_km and cutoff_km), converted to mph and multiplied by the gust factor. Gaps in a stored track are not bridged.
wind_model.not_modeled: Forward-motion asymmetry, terrain roughness, and any weakening over land beyond what the track's max_wind_kt already carries.

storm_catalog.source_wind_metric_note: One-minute sustained wind at the storm CENTRE in knots, HURDAT2 convention. This is not wind at a property and it is not a gust. Converting it to a property-level peak gust is app/wind.py's job, and that conversion is an assumption.
storm_catalog.completeness_warning: A SELECTED subset, not a probabilistic sample: these storms were chosen because they hit Florida hard. Do not compute annual expected loss, average annual loss or exceedance probabilities from it. That needs the full catalog and the annual event rates Adryel owns.

storm_size.source_note: hurdat2-radii-fit-v1: RMW from the storm's peak of 148.4 kt at 23.7412 N; decay and taper are record-wide medians. Not validated against station observations.
